articles.title: Why 3dfx 1 cards had such a washed out color output?
articles.summary: NeXTStation Colors and 3DFX cards had a washed out color output due to their use of 4 bits per channel and 5 or 6 bits per channel, which resulted in a non-linear display system. This meant that the colors were not accurately represented, leading to a "washed out" appearance in textures and render targets. The problem was exacerbated by the fact that artists created their textures in paint programs on conventional non-linear displays, resulting in a characteristic "washed out color" look.

articles.title: Squircles
articles.summary: Squircles are shapes intermediate between a square and a circle, with no single mathematical definition but various curves that fit the shape. The superellipse, popularized by Piet Hein, has the formula |x|^n + |y|^n = 1, and its gauge is the midpoint of the quadrant with a unit radius. Squircles can be created using either a single analytic curve or a mixture of straight line segments with corners, and their variation is controlled by the length of the flat side. The Apple squircle shape, with a gauge of 0.809, is a flat-sided squircle with a fixed length of flat side, and its flaws, such as an extraneous straight line segment and lack of symmetry, are minor.

articles.title: Paint in the memory of other programs
articles.summary: Paint in the memory of other programs constructs a visual representation of program memory, allowing users to manipulate and scribble on it. The program uses a Z-order curve to arrange pages of memory, with each pixel representing a bit. The bits are arranged in rows and columns, and the program can display different textures and patterns based on the data in memory. This can be useful for debugging and understanding complex programs, and can also be used to visualize data structures and programming patterns.
